message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm the asshole in this situation. Let me start by understanding what happened. A few years ago, I was renting a place with this dude, and we were on a lease. When the lease was ending, he just left without giving much notice. He took most of his stuff, leaving only the last bit of his half of the rent and a few things he didn't want to bring with him. Now, where I live, if you don't get rid of your stuff when you move out, the landlord can pay someone to remove it, and that cost comes out of your deposit. I've heard of people losing $250 just because someone had to take three milk crates of their stuff to the dump. It's a rip-off. So, I tried to contact him for two weeks, texting and emailing, asking him to pick up his stuff or let me take them to the dump. But he never responded. I ended up taking most of his stuff to the dump, but he had around 60 video games for the PS4. I thought, why not sell them? There's a local game store that buys used games, and they gave me $600 for all of his games. Fast forward to last week, I was at a party where he was also present, and we were being polite. Then he asked how the move-out process went, and I said it was good. Naturally, he asked what I did with his stuff. When he found out I sold his games, he got mad. I told him that I tried to get him to grab those things, but he never reached out. Now he's calling me an asshole and asking me to pay him back. I checked, and legally, there's nothing wrong with what I did. But now I'm wondering if I'm the asshole for doing this. Okay, so to figure this out, I need to consider a few things. First, was it reasonable for me to sell his games without his consent? Second, was it fair for me to keep the money from selling his games? Third, should I have handled the situation differently? Let's start with the first point: selling his games without his consent. When he moved out, he left his stuff behind, and I tried to contact him to let him know about the move-out process and the potential costs. He didn't respond, so I took the initiative to get rid of his stuff to avoid him losing money from his deposit. Selling the games was a way to recover some value from his belongings instead of just throwing them away. But on the other hand, selling his games without his permission might be seen as overstepping. Even though I tried to contact him, maybe I should have made more effort to inform him about the sale or at least ask for his permission. Moving on to the second point: keeping the money from selling his games. I used the money to cover some of the costs associated with moving out, but legally, I don't think I was obligated to give him the money back. However, ethically, if I sold his games, should I have given him the proceeds? Lastly, should I have handled the situation differently? Maybe I could have stored his games somewhere and waited longer for him to respond before selling them. Or perhaps I could have reached out to him through different channels to ensure he was aware of the situation. Overall, while I didn't do anything legally wrong, there might be some ethical considerations here. I might have been too quick to sell his games without ensuring he was aware and had the chance to retrieve them. It's possible that he feels wronged because he didn't get a chance to make decisions about his own belongings. In the end, I think there's a balance between being responsible and respecting someone's property rights. I might have leaned too much on the responsible side without fully considering his perspective. Maybe I should have found a middle ground, like holding onto his games longer or finding another way to handle the situation that respects both our interests.
